Many upstream inputs are not discussed because of limited supply chain information or relatively low importance (for inputs such as dopants, glue, and chemicals). • Polysilicon: See Section 2.6. • Quartz crucibles: The Quartz Corporation and Sibelco mines in Spruce Pine, North Carolina, provide some of the world’s highest-purity quartz, which is used in some high- temperature quartz crucibles. However, quartz crucibles for PV are almost exclusively produced in China. French-headquartered Saint Gobain makes quartz crucibles for semiconductor applications, which typically use smaller ingots than PV does. • Diamond wire: Chinese companies dominate diamond wire production for large-scale PV. In the past, there were suppliers headquartered in Japan (Asahi, Nakamura), Europe (Meyer Burger), and the United States (Diamond Materials Technology in Colorado, which was acquired by Meyer Burger). • Equipment: Chinese companies dominate PV ingot and wafer production equipment. Japan, South Korea, and Taiwan have semiconductor ingot and wafer equipment suppliers. Semiconductor and large-diameter PV ingot and wafer equipment is available in Europe (e.g., PVA TePla, Lapmaster, Wolters, Rena), but European manufacturers have been unable to finance scale-up because of uncertainty about demand for non- Chinese products. In the past, U.S.-headquartered Applied Materials periodically sold cropping and squaring and wafer slicing equipment from 2007 to 2015, from their 31 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. Precision Wafering Systems subsidiary in Switzerland. GT Advanced Technologies, also headquartered in the United States, designed, built, and sold Cz and multicrystalline ingot growth furnaces from around 2012 to 2016. Linton Crystal Technologies in Rochester, New York, sold Cz-growth equipment over many years since its formation in 1954. It is now part of Chinese-headquartered Dalian Linton and is the most recent firm with U.S. operations and capabilities to provide Cz, brick shaping, and wafering equipment for PV. At the end of 2024, the company’s U.S. presence was expected to come to a complete close by Q1 2026. This step of the c-Si supply chain is most reliant on China, considering manufacturing capacities in China and ownership of ingot and wafer facilities in ASEAN.
